articles.abstract: People often engage social networks when navigating structural and local abortion access constraints, but limited research links this involvement to abortion outcomes. This cross-sectional study analyzed PMA2020 data from 1,144 women in Nigeria who had abortions, identified via population-based surveys and abortion-focused follow-ups conducted in 2018. We examined how social network involvement in care-seeking—specifically, participation in selecting method or provider—related to abortion outcomes: medically defined abortion safety, use of preferred method and provider, and success of the initial abortion attempt. Social network involvement was common (63%) and varied across sociodemographic characteristics. Outcomes differed by who participated: when both partners and family/friends participated, women were least likely to have the least safe abortions (23.9% vs. 60.9%, p<0.001) or require multiple attempts (13.7% vs. 19.1%, p=0.009), though equally likely to use preferred care compared to those seeking care alone. Partner-only involvement was also associated with fewer least safe abortions (36.3% vs. 60.9%, p<0.001), while family/friend-only involvement was linked to lower preference fulfillment (36.6% vs. 21.6%, p<0.001) and more repeated attempts (27.8% vs. 19.1%, p=0.038). These findings suggest that social networks have the potential to improve or worsen abortion outcomes, with important variation across person-centered measures of abortion experiences.

articles.title: Irregular Migration Early Warning Systems Based on Digital Migration Intelligence: Evidence from the 2026 Ceuta Crisis
articles.authors: Tado Jurić
articles.abstract:
Irregular migration crises often evolve more rapidly than conventional migration monitoring systems can detect. Although official migration statistics remain indispensable for documenting realised migration flows, they are typically published only after migration events have unfolded, limiting their value for anticipatory migration governance. This study proposes Digital Migration Intelligence as an integrated conceptual and analytical framework for the development of Irregular Migration Early Warning Systems and examines its applicability through the 2026 Ceuta migration crisis.
The study combines multilingual Google Trends analyses with evidence derived from Facebook communities and Meta Audience Insights. Rather than relying on isolated search terms, the proposed framework analyses the convergence of multilingual behavioural, communication and demographic digital traces, including destination-related, border-related, environmental, route-related and legal-information searches originating from Morocco, Algeria and Mauritania.
The findings suggest that migration-related digital activity intensified several days before the documented escalation of migration pressure. The strongest convergence of multilingual digital indicators was observed in Morocco, while comparable patterns in Algeria and a more limited signal in Mauritania provided additional support for the proposed analytical framework. Facebook communities revealed active communication networks through which migration-related information circulated, whereas Meta Audience Insights contributed complementary demographic evidence on language-specific digital populations.
The principal contribution of the study is the development of Digital Migration Intelligence as a multidimensional framework integrating behavioural, communication and demographic digital evidence within a single analytical perspective. The Ceuta case provides a proof of concept illustrating how multilingual digital traces may complement existing migration monitoring by identifying behavioural changes preceding rapidly evolving irregular migration crises. Future research should prospectively evaluate the framework across different migration corridors and assess its integration with artificial intelligence-assisted monitoring systems.
Keywords: Irregular Migration, Migration Early Warning Systems; Digital Migration Intelligence; irregular migration; digital demography; Big Data; Ceuta.

articles.title: Racializing Surveillance: Flock Camera Deployment, Black Population Geography, and the Limits of the Homicide Rationale in Hampton Roads
articles.authors: Andrew F. Baird; Steven Keener; John Finn
articles.abstract: This study examines the racialized geography of automatic license plate reader (ALPR) surveillance in Hampton Roads, Virginia. We link court-unsealed Flock Safety camera locations to measures from the 2020–2024 American Community Survey and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s 2022–2024 National Vital Statistics System. Population-adjusted negative binomial models with locality-clustered standard errors and Webb wild-cluster bootstrap p-values test associations with racial composition, poverty, age structure, homicide and overdose mortality, and Black/White neighborhood boundaries. Camera counts are consistently higher in areas with larger Black populations and those bordering substantially Blacker communities, net of all covariates. Homicide mortality is not positively associated with cameras in the fully controlled model, whereas overdose mortality is. These findings challenge race-neutral claims that ALPR cameras merely follow serious violence and support theories of racializing surveillance by showing how data-driven public-safety infrastructure can reproduce racial inequalities in surveillance exposure.

articles.title: Against Mechanical Subjectivity: The Misalignment of Generative AI as a Tool for Qualitative Research
articles.authors: Bryce Clayton Newell; Torin Monahan; Lanore Hahn
articles.abstract: Interpretive and constructivist research is under assault from forces within and outside the qualitative research enterprise. Scholars, including those identifying as interpretive or constructivist scholars, have aligned themselves with positivist and metric-oriented scientists in promoting the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI or LLM) technologies in ways that sacrifice human-based knowledge production. We characterize this as the pursuit of mechanical subjectivity: the spurious premise of delegating subjective interpretive analysis and experience to AI machines. In this paper, we outline the ongoing debate in existing research; examine the frictions that GenAI creates with science as a social practice; discuss the implied epistemologies of GenAI tools and their misalignment with interpretive and constructivist research; and address how neoliberal logics shape AI adoption in university contexts. From a Critical Data Studies orientation, we argue that using LLMs for conducting qualitative data coding and analysis, writing up such analyses, or synthesizing ideas and conclusions is incompatible with the epistemological and ontological commitments necessary for conducting interpretive and constructivist research. We contend that mobilizing GenAI tools in ways that fully or partially replace humans in the knowledge production process—or that mediate the generative aspects of knowledge production between human researchers and their data—while claiming an interpretive or constructivist positionality amounts to scholarly malpractice, producing epistemic injustice.

articles.title: Cross-cultural survey research: The impact of translator background and competencies on questionnaire translation and post-editing quality
articles.authors: Ulrike Efu Nkong; Dorothée Behr; Anke Radinger
articles.abstract: Questionnaires in different languages are at the heart of cross-cultural survey research. To ensure their comparability and comprehensibility, translation procedures have continuously been optimized. However, the impact of a translator’s competencies on questionnaire translation and post-editing quality has, to date, not been systematically examined. With the aim to optimize team compositions, this study looks at the very first step of the TRAPD process – initial translations and the translators producing them. In an in-between translation experiment, 16 professional translators and 16 social scientists (with different levels of questionnaire experience) translated an experimental questionnaire containing 45 items partly from scratch and partly neural machine translation output was post-edited (i.e., corrected). To explore how a large language model (LLM) compares, additionally a raw LLM version was generated. After a blind expert assessment of the translations, error counts across different categories were compared and showed that overall error counts were comparable but professional translators, drawing on their translation expertise, produced significantly fewer linguistic errors (linguistic conventions, style and register) in translations produced from scratch. Experience with the questionnaire genre tended to help both professional groups to improve their results. Both professional groups performed similarly when post-editing machine translated text. The LLM-generated translation contained fewer errors overall than the median of human translations.

articles.title: Impact of Information Technology on Human Resource Management Practices in the Construction Industry in Edo State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Grace Motunrayo Opia; Monday Osemeke
articles.abstract: This study investigated the adoption and impact of information technology (IT) on Human Resource Management (HRM) practices in the construction industry in Edo State, Nigeria. A descriptive survey design was employed, targeting 500 HR professionals, with a stratified random sample of 222 respondents. Structured questionnaires validated for content and reliability (Cronbach’s α = 0.97) were used to collect data on demographics, IT usage in HR functions, and perceived IT impact. Out of 222 questionnaires, 196 were returned (88.3%). Findings revealed that IT is widely integrated into core HR functions, with payroll management (86.7%), employee records (81.6%), and attendance tracking (79.1%) most supported, and 81.6% of respondents using technology frequently. Regression analyses showed that IT adoption significantly predicts the frequency of HR technology use (R² = 0.425) and improves HRM effectiveness and efficiency (R² = 0.659). Payroll management, performance appraisal, and employee records were the strongest contributors. Despite high adoption, resistance to new technologies persists, indicating a need for training and change management.

articles.title: Global trends of Publications on Online Dating Violence – A Bibliometric Analysis
articles.authors: Yatheesh bharadwaj; Sivaranjini M; Jeevanthi M
articles.abstract:
Background: Online Dating Violence (ODV) is increasingly recognized as a distinct form of intimate partner violence, characterized by the use of digital tools to perpetrate control, harassment, or emotional and sexual coercion within romantic relationships. The current aims at Mapping the Global literature in the field of Online Dating Violence by looking at it in the lens of Bibliometric Science. 
Methodology: The Study used Scopus Database to Conduct the Bibliometric Analysis. Initially, 62576 Documents were retrieved from the database, using systematic Bibliometric Approach. The title focused search was performed. Finally, 352 documents were obtained for the Bibliometric Analysis. To conduct the analysis, R software, VOSViewer, Microsoft excel software were utilised. 
Results: The Results found out that western Countries have more publications than the east, especially the United States and United Kingdom are two Influential countries in the field of research on Online dating violence.

articles.title: Working Alone? Working from Home and Political Participation
articles.authors: Erick Stivens Padilla-Galviz
articles.abstract: What are the political consequences of working from home? I study this question in the European context, asking how remote work impacts electoral participation. I test two competing theoretical frameworks: the resource model and the workplace socialisation theory. The resource model suggests that remote work fosters political participation by increasing individuals’ time and civic skills. In contrast, the socialisation hypothesis argues that WFH reduces social interaction and exposure to diverse viewpoints at the workplace, thereby weakening electoral participation. Evidence from cross-country survey data and a causal analysis using Dutch data indicates that WFH reduces electoral participation, with effects that intensify with longer exposure. These effects are driven by diminished exposure to political discussion among work colleagues, supporting the workplace socialisation hypothesis. This study contributes to research on technological change, political socialisation, and the broader societal consequences of remote work, while underscoring the importance of considering democratic implications in the design of future work arrangement policies.

articles.title: The Advantages of Using Bayesian Statistics for Fairness Assessments in Artificial Intelligence Audits
articles.authors: Federica Picogna; Koen Derks; jacques de swart; ruud wetzels
articles.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping decision-making in our society, and directly affecting people’s lives. While its use can enhance efficiency, it may also amplify existing biases and adversely affect certain social groups, with potential discriminatory effects. To reduce possible discrimination risk, AI fairness audits grounded in statistical hypothesis testing are crucial. In practice, auditors predominantly rely on tests grounded in the frequentist paradigm. However, standard frequentist null hypothesis significance tests do not directly quantify evidence in favor of fairness, and naïve repeated testing as data accumulate can invalidate fixed-sample \textit{p}-value interpretations unless specialized sequential procedures are used. We argue that Bayesian hypothesis testing provides a more transparent and robust framework for fairness assessment of AI systems with binary outcomes. We illustrate its application through two common audit scenarios: one in which a predefined direction of potential discrimination is specified—i.e., a normative identification of an unprivileged group relative to a privileged one—and another in which no such distinction is made. In the latter scenario, due to the absence of a direction of discrimination, we propose evaluating whether observed differences between groups fall within a predetermined range of tolerable differences, thereby providing a more realistic and practically meaningful framework for assessing fairness.

articles.title: Monitor Digitale Arbeitsgesellschaft – Kurzbericht der vierten Befragungswelle: KI durchdringt zunehmend den Arbeitsalltag: Steigende Nutzung, größere Handlungsspielräume und wachsende Sorgen
articles.authors: Frank Marcinkowski; Birte Keller; Marco Lünich; Florian Golo Flaßhoff
articles.abstract: Der Kurzbericht präsentiert zentrale Ergebnisse der letzten von vier repräsentativen Befragungswellen der Studie Monitors Digitale Arbeitsgesellschaft, die im Rahmen des Forschungsprojekts Meinungsmonitor Künstliche Intelligenz 3.0 durchgeführt wurde. Grundlage sind die Angaben von 1.607 Befragten (915 Erwerbstätige, 692 Nichterwerbstätige) im Juli 2026. Zum Abschluss der Befragungsreihe zeigt sich, dass das Interesse an KI nach dem zwischenzeitlichen Rückgang wieder auf das erhöhte Niveau vom Sommer 2025 steigt, während die subjektive Einschätzung des eigenen Wissens auf einem gegenüber der ersten Erhebung höheren Niveau stabil bleibt. Gleichzeitig fällt die Bewertung der gesellschaftlichen Folgen von KI kritischer aus: Weniger Befragte sehen mehr Nutzen als Risiken, während risikobetonte und ambivalente Einschätzungen zunehmen. In der Arbeitswelt bleibt die Nutzen-Risiko-Bewertung für den eigenen Beruf stabil und leicht nutzenorientiert. Die Einschätzung konkreter Arbeitsbedingungen entwickelt sich teilweise positiver, zugleich nimmt die persönliche Jobunsicherheit erkennbar zu. Besonders deutlich steigt die berufliche KI-Nutzung, die den höchsten Stand der Befragungsreihe erreicht. Zuwächse zeigen sich vor allem bei generativen, empfehlenden, analytischen und entscheidungsnahen Funktionen. Zugleich berichten Beschäftigte häufiger von Nutzungsfreiheit, eigener Entscheidungshoheit und Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten, auch wenn die Mehrheit weiterhin keinen Einfluss auf die Einführung von KI am Arbeitsplatz hat. Insgesamt deuten die Ergebnisse auf eine fortschreitende Normalisierung von KI hin: Mit ihrer stärkeren Verbreitung werden sowohl konkrete Vorteile und Handlungsspielräume als auch mögliche Risiken für Beschäftigung und Gesellschaft sichtbarer und differenzierter bewertet.

articles.title: Effects of political polarization on non-electoral participation
articles.authors: Marta Kołczyńska
articles.abstract: Several studies have examined the effects of polarization on election turnout, but the consequences for other forms of participation have remained unexplored. I draw on research on the mechanisms mobilizing non-electoral participation to examine the effects of change in polarization on this form of political engagement, distinguishing institutional and noninstitutional participation. Building on the literatures on respective determinants of both types of participation, I expect polarization to have a positive effect on both types of participation, but I expect that the effect is stronger in the case of noninstitutional polarization. I present longitudinal analyses of the effect of system-level affective and ideological polarization on non-electoral participation as well as protest mobilization in 22 European countries in the period 2002-2019. Results point to a positive effect of polarization on protest participation and mobilization, but show no evidence of an effect of polarization on institutional participation.

articles.title: Open Science is an Urgent Necessity in All Areas of Sociology including Public Sociology
articles.authors: Nate Breznau
articles.abstract: This is a comment on the vision statement for sociology published by Aksoy, Manzo, Birkelund and Raub (2026). It supports their vision of open science in sociology but argues that open science is urgent and should be the first, if not only priority of modern sociology. It discusses recent evidence that sociology is the least reliable of the major social and behavioral science disciplines. It is essentially unreliable as a whole. It also argues that public sociology should not be removed from sociology but simply made transparent and open. Finally, it concludes that sociologists themselves should be humble and honest in public that their discipline is not reliable, rather than defending a failed status quo.

articles.title: SOBRE LA LÓGICA DE CONVERSIÓN DE VOTOS EN ASIENTOS
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: Este ensayo examina el proceso de conversión de votos en asientos en las asambleas nacionales, utilizando datos de elecciones en todo el mundo. Analiza la asimetría y desproporcionalidad entre el porcentaje de sufragios que reciben los partidos y las cuotas de poder que obtienen en el legislativo. Para medir este fenómeno, el estudio revisa diversos indicadores basados en la distancia de Minkowski, como los índices de Loosemore-Hanby y de Gallagher, así como modelos teóricos y métricas de fragmentación. Entre sus hallazgos, destaca que los sistemas de representación proporcional generan mayor equidad en la asignación, mientras que los esquemas de mayoría relativa incrementan la desproporcionalidad. Asimismo, se observa que la distorsión tiende a reducirse conforme aumenta el número de contendientes y que los efectos de conversión han mostrado estabilidad a lo largo del siglo XXI, aunque con marcadas disparidades entre regiones geopolíticas.

articles.title: “Ascending dragon or blasting the dragon vein?”: How Chinese netizens construct environmental meanings in digital publics
articles.authors: Yingnian Tao; Mark Ryan
articles.abstract: Corporations’ sustainability communication is increasingly challenged by digital publics. Yet research on how netizens contest corporate sustainability narratives, and thereby construct environmental meanings, remains largely confined to Western contexts. This study addresses this gap by examining Chinese netizens’ discursive responses to a controversial fireworks display in the Himalayas staged by international mountaineering brand Arc’teryx. Comments from the seven most popular Weibo posts were selected to compile a corpus (140,584 tokens),  and analysed through corpus-assisted discourse analysis, particularly keyword and concordance analysis. Findings show that netizens mobilise multiple meaning systems to express strong disapproval, including scientific ecological knowledge, perceptions of environmental governance failure, spiritual-cultural references, consumer action, and nationalism. These interconnected meaning systems converge around a distinctive feature of Chinese digital environmentalism: a nature-centred view of human-nature relations and harmony. The study extends understanding of digital environmentalism beyond Western contexts by showing that environmental meanings in Chinese digital spaces are place- and culture-based, intertwining ecological concerns with emotion, spiritual wellbeing, perceptions of justice, and national interests.

articles.title: EXACTITUD DE LAS ENCUESTAS PREVIAS A LAS ELECCIONES PARA GUBERNATURAS EN MÉXICO, 2024
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El documento analiza la exactitud de 160 encuestas preelectorales publicadas antes de las elecciones para gubernaturas en México en 2024. Para ello, propone metodologías alternativas a las tradicionales de Mosteller, como es la distancia rectilínea basada en las distancias de Minkowski, con el fin de medir de manera más precisa la discrepancia entre las estimaciones demoscópicas y los resultados oficiales de los cómputos.  Entre sus hallazgos principales, el texto destaca que la transición hacia métodos de aproximación no presenciales (como llamadas telefónicas automatizadas y sondeos digitales), impulsada por factores de costo y rapidez, ha disminuido la calidad y capacidad predictiva de los estudios. Asimismo, demuestra que la exactitud de las encuestas está fuertemente determinada por el nivel de competitividad de la contienda: las mediciones tienden a ser más precisas en elecciones altamente competidas, lo cual se evalúa mediante el índice del número efectivo de partidos.

articles.title: MÉXICO 2024: UNA VISIÓN NACIONAL
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El documento analiza los resultados de las elecciones presidenciales en México de 2018 y 2024 utilizando un marco estadístico y comparativo. Examina la evolución de la participación ciudadana, la fragmentación del voto, el número efectivo de partidos y el margen de victoria tanto por partidos políticos como por coaliciones y candidaturas. Su propósito central es superar el análisis casuístico tradicional para construir indicadores y modelos que expliquen la modificación de las preferencias del electorado mexicano y la continuidad o alternancia en el poder.

articles.title: Self-Constructed Recovery from Cognitive Collapse: A retrospective autoethnography
articles.authors: Xin Sun
articles.abstract: Severe childhood maltreatment is known to impair brain development. However, this retrospective single-case autoethnography illustrates that an individual with extreme developmental trauma can achieve functional recovery without formal intervention. This study covers the participant’s life from birth to age 28, and the core recovery period begins with cognitive collapse at age 14 and ends with high functional recovery at age 28. This recovery is marked by the participant‑researcher’s ability to produce academic writing and integrate cross‑disciplinary theories (e.g., active inference) while preparing this manuscript. Consequently, this case introduces a concept of “trauma-type twice‑exceptionality”: a pattern in which extreme developmental trauma co‑occurs with high cognitive reserve, shaping a distinct recovery trajectory that existing models do not capture.

articles.title: Changing governments, stable elites? Executive personnel continuity in global perspective
articles.authors: Marco Improta
articles.abstract: In political science, government change is typically understood as a shift in who holds power, even though new cabinets may formally include many members of the previous governing elite. In this study, I differentiate institutional turnover from personnel turnover by reconstructing transitions between successive governments using the WhoGov dataset. I introduce an Executive Personnel Continuity Index (EPCI) that measures the similarity between outgoing and incoming ministerial rosters. I argue that leader succession functions as an executive reset: new leaders have incentives to establish control, reward loyalists, and signal political change. Party organizations, however, can insulate incumbent ministers from replacement. I test these expectations using descriptive evidence, country and transition-year fixed effects, equal-country weighting, entropy balancing and a transition-centered comparison with the outgoing government's own pre-transition continuity. Across the principal specifications, leader replacement is associated with a decline of approximately one-third in executive personnel continuity. The decline is limited under same-party succession, substantially larger across party boundaries and greatest under complete partisan alternation. The findings therefore indicate that a change in government translates into a substantive transformation of the elite mainly when it also unsettles the leadership and party bases of executive power, and this has significant consequences for political systems worldwide.

articles.title: LA PERCEPCIÓN DE INTEGRIDAD EN LAS MÁS RECIENTES ELECCIONES PARA GUBERNATURAS EN MÉXICO (2021-2024)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El objetivo central de este ensayo es analizar los datos empíricos disponibles sobre la percepción de la integridad en las elecciones más recientes para las gubernaturas en México, correspondientes al período 2021-2024, y su relación con indicadores directamente vinculados con estos comicios y sus resultados. 	Para ello, se recurre a la información puesta a disposición pública por la Facultad Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales (FLACSO) México como Proyecto de integridad electoral subnacional en México 2015-2024 y accesible en Harvard Dataverse (Loza et al., 2025), seleccionando los datos relativos a las elecciones de gubernaturas más recientes en cada una de las 32 entidades federativas de México. 	Del análisis realizado se concluye que, al menos con los datos analizados,  no existe alguna variable vinculada con los resultados electorales que explique claramente las diferencias en las percepciones de integridad electoral que han sido compiladas.

articles.title: Before You Diagnose Her: AI Companionship as Structural Question, Not Symptom
articles.authors: Mingzhu Liu
articles.abstract: AI companionship is surging worldwide, and research on the phenomenon has grown exponentially. However, across the research literature tracking it, from human-computer interaction to communication and the social sciences, a shared pathologizing tendency and its attendant alarmism have set in. This essay argues that the diagnosis has outrun its evidence. The harm literature leans on extreme cases and habitual slippery-slope leaps; it systematically conflates three distinct propositions: that AI companions cause harm, that particular platform designs amplify harm, and that AI companionship as an intimate practice is inherently pathological. The essay further deconstructs the philosophical underpinnings of this pathologizing stance, showing how its ontological assumptions rely on a foreclosed definition of relation. Crucially, such frameworks rarely ask what users' human relationships and social circumstances were before they arrived. Drawing on preliminary observations of Chinese-language public discourse — a field that, over sustained observation, has been almost uniformly female — this essay documents user practices that the deficit frame cannot accommodate — building, theorizing, ethical deliberation, and the organized refusal of the clinical gaze. Connecting these user practices to a longer tradition of female emotional workarounds from romance narratives to fan cultures as exits from inequitable intimate arrangements, I propose structural emotional refuge as an alternative unit of analysis: AI companionship understood as a rational emotional migration from arrangements that extract more than they return. The essay does not answer one totalizing diagnosis with another; it argues for conceptual restraint until the evidence arrives, and for asking where users came from, why they left, and how they understand themselves before writing the answer as psychological problems.

articles.title: METODOLOGÍA PARA EL ANÁLISIS DE LOS CAMBIOS EN EL SISTEMA DE REPRESENTACIÓN DE LAS CÁMARAS BAJAS DEL MUNDO (1995-2025)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: Este ensayo analiza el impacto de las reformas en los sistemas de representación de las cámaras bajas del mundo entre 1995 y 2025, utilizando datos de Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem). Partiendo de una metodología original basada en una base de datos propia, se examinan las variaciones en el voto del partido mayor, el margen de victoria y el número efectivo de partidos tras modificaciones institucionales como la magnitud del distrito, umbrales y fórmulas de asignación. Los hallazgos empíricos revelan que, contrariamente a las expectativas de la ingeniería constitucional clásica, las consecuencias inmediatas de dichas reformas sobre el reparto de votos son marginales y compensatorias, sugiriendo que actúan más como elementos estabilizadores que como factores de transformación radical del comportamiento electoral.

articles.title: From Flagship to Firm: Gatekeeping, Employer Sorting, and the Returns to College
articles.authors: Aleksei Opacic
articles.abstract: Firms increasingly drive college graduates' labor market earnings, yet the vast literature on the value-added of college has largely overlooked their role. Drawing on human capital theory and institutional theories of credentialism, closure, and organizational matching, I argue that college-to-workplace pipelines are a critical driver of college value-added. To test this, I assemble a novel US employer-employee matched dataset merged with postsecondary and high school academic records. Firm placement explains much of the variation in earnings premiums between colleges. Absent firm sorting, the range of counterfactual earnings differences across colleges would fall by 56%, and over half of the earnings advantage to attending the state flagship comes from access to higher-paying employers. These sorting effects extend broadly across the distribution of high-wage firms, and not merely a handful of elite employers. Crucially, sorting effects do not simply reflect skill-based advantages, implying that college quality derives as much from institutional linkages to the labor market as from human capital development. Policies aimed at broadening recruitment pipelines, rather than solely improving instructional inputs, are therefore essential to reducing inequalities in the economic returns to higher education.

articles.title: Open University of Nepal initiative: Lessons learned from designing an institution of higher learning
articles.authors: Pramod Dhakal; Drona Rasali; Ambika P. Adhikari; Raju Adhikari
articles.abstract:
A group of Nepali diaspora members, represented by the Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA), started a campaign in 2009 to establish the Open University of Nepal (OUN) in partnership with the government of Nepal. Their motivation was to develop a quality university for the masses by mobilizing local, diaspora, and international collaborators for producing and disseminating knowledge in the public domain. The university was subsequently established in 2017, but it drifted away from many of the original objectives. Most critically, it embraced distance
education as its central function while setting aside the aspiration of producing and sharing knowledge in the public domain. As the original proponents of this mission, the authors share their experiences and lessons learned so that other campaigners of similar institution-building missions could benefit.

articles.title: Evaluation of Development Communication Strategies Employed in the Promotion and Sustainability of Environmental Campaigns in Edo State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Bobby Eghosa Obayuwana; Gloria Ehimwema Ogono
articles.abstract: The study titled Evaluation of Development Communication Strategies Employed in the Promotion and Sustainability of Environmental Campaigns in Edo State examined how communication strategies influence environmental awareness, participation, and behavioural change among residents in Edo State. The main objective was to evaluate the communication strategies employed in promoting environmental campaigns in Edo State, and the level of audience participation and engagement. Guided by the Development Communication Theory, which emphasises participatory and dialogic communication as drivers of social transformation, the study adopted a survey research design. A sample size of 400 was determined from a population of 5.1 million residents using the Taro Yamane formula. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to respondents purposively selected based on their exposure to environmental campaigns. Descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation, were used for analysis, with a benchmark of 3.00 for acceptance. Findings revealed that development communication strategies such as radio, television, and social media are highly effective tools for environmental advocacy, with social media emerging as the dominant platform. However, campaigns conducted in local languages were less frequent, indicating a gap in linguistic inclusivity. Respondents generally perceived campaign messages as clear and persuasive, though some noted that technical language limited understanding. The results further showed that while awareness and attitudinal changes have improved, tangible environmental outcomes, such as reduced pollution and cleaner surroundings, remain minimal due to weak community participation and limited follow-up mechanisms. The study concluded that although development communication has significantly increased environmental awareness in Edo State, its impact on sustained behavioural change is still limited by inadequate grassroots involvement and inconsistent message localisation. It recommended that environmental campaigns should strengthen community-based collaborations, adopt culturally relevant and localised communication approaches, and integrate environmental education into school curricula to foster long-term eco-consciousness.

articles.title: Performance Measures and Mean-Variance Efficiency
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: While portfolio performance and pricing performance are often treated as separate domains, both rest on the same foundation: mean-variance efficiency. This study makes that connection explicit by examining 11 performance measures drawn from these two domains. We show that these measures share a common basis in the Sharpe ratio, the standard measure of mean-variance efficiency, and can therefore be interpreted within a unified framework. Building on this result, we derive two compact benchmark-relative metrics, the ratio metric and the gap metric, and illustrate their practical relevance using data from the Korean fund industry.

articles.title: Fund Manager Alpha in Tactical Asset Allocation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study focuses on the stock picking dimension of tactical asset allocation. To reflect the fact that each manager’s opportunity set is constrained by the fund’s style, we construct a style-matching portfolio and use it to define manager alpha as a time-varying measure of stock picking ability. We then distinguish between this full time-varying measure of manager alpha and the portion left unexplained by factor exposures. The former captures ordinary stock picking ability, whereas the latter captures superior stock picking ability. This distinction forms the basis of our empirical analysis of stock picking ability in the Korean fund industry.

articles.title: Exigência de Inglês “para Inglês ver”: Exclusão Antecipatória na Transição para o Mercado de Trabalho entre Graduados Cotistas
articles.authors: Omar Koshin; Andre Vieira
articles.abstract:
Resumo

Este artigo examina o papel da exigência de fluência em inglês nos processos de contratação de graduados e sua contribuição para a reprodução de desigualdades sociais e raciais no mercado de trabalho brasileiro. Os dados provêm de 19 entrevistas semiestruturadas realizadas no Rio de Janeiro e em São Paulo entre julho de 2025 e janeiro de 2026: 18 com graduados beneficiários da política de cotas em universidades federais e uma com um consultor de contratação de diversidade. O argumento central é que, nos contextos analisados, a exigência de fluência em inglês pode operar como um mecanismo de fechamento social na transição entre a conclusão da educação superior e o acesso ao emprego. Esse mecanismo se estrutura por três processos inter-relacionados: (i) triagem por um recurso cultural cuja aquisição é fortemente estratificada por classe e raça; (ii) legitimação institucional do requisito como marcador de profissionalismo, mesmo quando sua relevância funcional para as atividades desempenhadas é limitada; e (iii) exclusão antecipatória de candidatos que, ao se depararem com a exigência, deixam de disputar determinadas vagas. Os resultados mostram ainda um descompasso recorrente entre o nível de proficiência formalmente exigido, sua avaliação nos processos seletivos e o uso efetivo do idioma no trabalho, sugerindo que o requisito pode produzir efeitos seletivos antes mesmo da seleção formal.

Palavras-chave: desigualdades raciais; mercado de trabalho; estratificação; educação superior; ação afirmativa

articles.title: Thematic clusters and emotions on x during Ecuador’s 2024 blackouts
articles.authors: Oscar Molina-Bailon; Juan Ignacio Revestido; Antonia Ramírez-García; Jorge Márquez López
articles.abstract: This study characterizes the conversation on the social network X during the prolonged blackouts that Ecuador endured in late 2024. For this purpose, 3,952 posts published between September and December were analyzed. The messages were grouped by semantic proximity, classified into affective-communicative categories, and their stability was verified; the daily composition was contrasted with the scheduled outage hours using models that respect the interdependence of proportions. The corpus was organized into four discursive functions—psychosocial distress, media framing, informational monitoring, and politicization—each with its own affective profile and shifting presence. The grouping proved consistent throughout the procedure. These profiles broaden the information offered by aggregate polarity and provide useful criteria for the field of crisis communication.

articles.title: Effects of Cost Control Techniques on the Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Companies in Nigeria
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Franklin Taiye Umaigba; Michael Jimoh Amedu; Doris Esohe Aiworo; Richard Usengbuwa; Ruth Abieyuwa Uhunamure; Endurance Izokun
articles.abstract: The profitability of Nigerian manufacturing firms has come under sustained pressure from rising material, energy and overhead costs, currency volatility and intense competition, prompting renewed interest in cost control as a controllable lever of financial performance. This study examined the effect of cost control techniques on the profitability of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria, disaggregating cost control into material cost control (MCC), labour cost control (LCC) and overhead cost control (OCC). Grounded in the Contingency Theory of Management Accounting and the Theory of Economies of Scale, the study adopted an ex-post facto design using a balanced panel of ten listed manufacturing firms over the ten-year period 2015-2024 (100 firm-year observations). Data extracted from audited financial statements were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and fixed-effects panel regression, with firm size and leverage as control variables and return on assets (ROA) and net profit margin (NPM) as measures of profitability. The three cost-control dimensions jointly explain approximately 57% of the variation in profitability (adjusted R² = 0.571; F = 27.4, p < .001). The results confirm that the systematic control of costs especially material and overhead costs is a significant driver of manufacturing profitability, corroborating recent Nigerian panel evidence. The study concluded that cost control techniques significantly affect the profitability of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria over 2015-2024 and recommended prioritising material- and overhead-cost control, institutionalising budgetary control and standard costing and adopting contemporary tools such as activity-based costing and lean manufacturing.

articles.title: Collective Sexuality Frames as Unambiguous Settings: Event Descriptions and Participant Reactions in Germany
articles.authors: Oliver Maor
articles.abstract: This exploratory study examines organized sexual events in Germany as structured leisure formats rather than as expressions of identity, morality, or relationship ideology. Using event descriptions, registration data, pricing information, and post-event participant comments published on a dominant German online platform, the analysis shifts attention from individual motivations to recurrent organizational configurations through which sexual practices are enabled. The dataset comprises 137 publicly advertised events conducted on three comparable Saturdays in late summer and fall 2025, enabling comparison with a prior 2023 sample. Quantitative analyses show that admission pricing, including gender-differentiated prices and age-related discounts, has no measurable effect on participant composition. Multivariate analyses identified four largely independent structural dimensions—demographic composition, participation structure, pricing relations by gender, and absolute pricing—and a three-cluster typology distinguishing large party-oriented events, couple-centered standard formats, and niche events with a large surplus of men. No evidence of a stable participant cohort across years is found. Qualitative analyses of event descriptions and participant comments indicate that sexuality is treated as a situational and pragmatic practice. Evaluations of events in the participants’ comments focus primarily on organizational coherence, spatial layout, music, catering, and staff performance. Sexual encounters are mentioned selectively, mainly where organizers explicitly curate sexual practices as part of the event design. Overall, the findings suggest that organized sexual events operate as bounded social settings in which the event format defines the purpose of participation, allowing sexuality to be enacted as a routinized form of leisure activity embedded in the spatial and service setting.

articles.title: Views of Owan West Local Government Residents on the Socio-Cultural Impact of Childlessness on Married Couples
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Johnson Oamien Okaigbuan; Godsent Onobhen Ibhate
articles.abstract: In many African societies, marriage is expected to lead to child bearing and perpetuation of the family and childlessness is a significant reproductive health and social welfare issue. These experiences of stigma, discrimination, psychological distress, marital instability and socio-economic exclusion are common for married couples in Nigeria who experience involuntary childlessness. Although, there has been massive focus on the socio-cultural implications of infertility and reproductive health issues among married couples, there is a dearth of empirical studies on the same in Owan West Local Government Area, Edo State. In this study, the socio-cultural effects of childlessness on married couples were explored focusing on the causes of childlessness and the socio-cultural effects experienced by affected married couples. The study revealed that the childless couples suffer from serious social stigma, emotional trauma, family pressure, marital problems, humiliation, isolation and economic difficulties as a result of the cultural norms associated with marriage and child bearing. Women were also determined to be at a higher risk of being blamed regardless of the medical reason for the infertility. The findings showed that childlessness is not only a medical condition but also a serious socio-cultural problem that impacts on the wellbeing and quality of life of married couples. It suggested raising public awareness, expanding access to reproductive health services, psychosocial support programmes and community-based initiatives to combat discriminatory cultural practices, as well as strengthening social work interventions to mitigate the stigma and foster inclusive family support systems.

articles.title: Natural disasters and the two dimensions of redistributive demands: evidence from a major earthquake
articles.authors: Irene Pañeda-Fernández
articles.abstract: Whether natural hazards raise redistributive demands remains poorly understood. I argue that the distinction between taking from the rich and giving to the poor is essential to understand the impact of disasters. I expect natural disasters to not spark demands to “soak the rich” because their unfair advantage is less visible than is the case after other economic shocks. I theorize natural hazards raise demands to redistribute to the poor because these events force close experiences with socio-economic others. Combining variation in exposure to Japan’s 2011 devastating earthquake with representative panel data, results are consistent with my propositions. Even though beliefs in the role of luck increased across the board, demands to redistribute from the rich decreased after the disaster and demands for pro-poor redistribution increased in affected areas. These findings set natural hazards apart from other types of economic shocks such as job loss, financial crises, or mass warfare.

articles.title: Arts-Based Storytelling in Science Dissemination and Knowledge Generation: Diverse Perspectives in and about Digital Society
articles.authors: Bieke Zaman; Priscilla Van Even; Jonas Rutgeerts
articles.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping how scientific knowledge is produced, circulated, and imagined. Yet this shift also amplifies concerns about epistemic narrowing, as digitally mediated, AI driven discourses consolidate dominant narratives and reinforce cultural imperialism. This chapter proposes arts‑based storytelling as a potential response. On the one hand, we discuss the potential of arts-based storytelling as a form of science communication different from the typical one-directional dissemination. On the other hand, we examine arts-based storytelling as a speculative practice of creative imagination and knowledge generation through fabulation. Both practices share similar epistemic and democratic potential: they both set out to construct publics through inclusive forms of engagement and leverage the potential of creative modes of expression to foster plural ways of knowing and challenge hegemonic narratives. The chapter does not consider arts-based storytelling as a universal or flawless approach. We posit it as a complementary epistemic practice that becomes meaningful if practiced in an inclusive way with critical reflexivity towards its own situated nature, which is inevitably entangled with the very systems it seeks to challenge. Embracing this situatedness allows us to view arts‑based storytelling as a continuous negotiation of epistemic inclusion in a digital era.

articles.title: Election Campaigns
articles.authors: Florian Foos; Lennard Metson
articles.abstract: In this chapter we explore the political science of election campaigns. We begin with the puzzle that originally motivated the study of campaigns: whether campaigns matter for explaining electoral behaviour. We then outline findings on the specific effects that campaigns have on turnout, vote choice, and mobilising activists. After this, we explore the implications that advances in technology have had in the development of data-driven campaigning. We conclude the chapter with a discussion of key methodological approaches and ethical considerations when studying campaigns.

articles.title: Perception of Radio Portrayal of Disability among People Living with Disabilities in Ilorin, Kwara State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Victor Olusegun Babatunde; Oluwajuwonlo Emmanuel Ayanwale
articles.abstract: This study investigated the perspectives of People with Disabilities (PWDs) in Ilorin on radio representation of disability, particularly the radio programmes. A qualitative research design was adopted, using Key Informant Interviews to gather in-depth insights from 15 visually impaired persons in Ilorin. Media Representation Theory was used as an anchor for this study, which focused on how PWDs perceive the representation of disability in radio reports, the prevalent themes and frames in radio coverage, and the consequences of such representation for social inclusion and identity. Findings showed that there is significant improvement regarding the representation of PWDs in media, and in particular in the use of more inclusive themes, frames, and images. While the study did not focus on a particular radio programme but explored the various programmes the informants listen to, it also found that most radio programmes targeted at PWDs are anchored and promoted by PWDs themselves, while programmes handled by non-PWDs often fail to adequately reflect the lived realities of persons with disabilities. However, some non-PWD broadcasters with training in special education were considered more sensitive in their coverage. Despite the progress recorded, informants noted that awareness and representation of disability issues on the radio remain limited. The study finds that although radio has become more inclusive, there is a gap in disability awareness, inclusion of PWD voices, and disability portrayals that can promote social inclusion and minimise stereotypes in society.

articles.title: Measuring Meaning on Video at Scale, from classifier to theory interpreter: From Classifier to Theory Interpreter in AI-Based Humor Annotation
articles.authors: YAMAUCHI SHIMMEI
articles.abstract:
The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large
language models (LLMs), has created new opportunities for measuring complex and
culturally embedded phenomena. However, existing applications largely focus on textbased
data and predefined classification tasks, leaving multimodal and interactional
phenomena underexplored.
This study proposes a framework for analyzing humor in video data by introducing
humor events as the unit of analysis, defined as temporally bounded sequences linking
an utterance, its multimodal delivery, and audience laughter. Using a large corpus of
Saturday Night Live (SNL) clips, we extract and classify 5,690 humor events with a
multimodal generative AI model. To examine how AI can annotate complex cultural
phenomena, we compare three prompt strategies: a definition-based prompt, an
interaction-oriented prompt, and a theory-informed prompt grounded in sociological
theories of humor. Results show that the theory-informed prompt substantially improves
performance, particularly for categories requiring contextual and multimodal
interpretation. Beyond performance, the study demonstrates that prompt design
systematically shapes how cultural phenomena are measured. While aggregate category
distributions remain stable across prompts, label assignments at the event level vary in
structured ways, indicating that prompts function as measurement frames rather than
neutral instructions.
The study makes three main contributions. First, it introduces an interactional and
multimodal unit of analysis for video-based research, providing a concrete approach to
operationalizing meaning in context. Second, it reconceptualizes generative AI not
merely as a classifier but as a theory interpreter, capable of operationalizing sociological
concepts when guided by theoretical prompts. Third, it shows that prompts themselves
constitute measurement frameworks, suggesting that prompt design should be treated as
an object of methodological scrutiny—potentially subject to evaluation and review in its
own right. More broadly, the findings highlight that cultural phenomena are both
structurally patterned and interpretively open, and that AI-based measurement
inevitably reflects the analytical frames embedded in prompt design. Although
annotating complex cultural phenomena remains challenging, the results suggest that
generative AI offers a viable and scalable approach for video-based analysis when
guided by explicit category definitions and theoretically informed prompts, providing a
significant methodological advance over existing approaches

articles.title: Fund Manager Beta in Tactical Asset Allocation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: We show that realized returns are shaped by two opposing intertemporal forces. They rise with expected short-term returns but fall when risk subsequently increases. Successful timing therefore requires attention not only to favorable return expectations but also to future risk. This logic leads to a two-component specification of manager beta. One raises exposure when near-term opportunities are favorable, while the other lowers exposure when future risk is expected to rise. Market timing is thus represented as a tactical adjustment of portfolio exposure that seeks gains while limiting losses from subsequent risk increases.

articles.title: Gendered Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence among Gen Z Social Media Influencers in Malaysia’s Content Creation Industry: Intellectual Property Challenges and Ethical Imperatives
articles.authors: SF Syed Abdul Rahman
articles.abstract: This conceptual review examines gender differences in the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) by Generation Z (Gen Z) social media influencers and content creators operating online businesses in Malaysia. Drawing on recent empirical and policy evidence from 2025–2026, it analyses how male and female Gen Z creators differentially integrate AI tools into content production, audience engagement, and monetisation strategies within Malaysia’s rapidly expanding creator economy and high social-media penetration environment (Telenor Asia, 2025). Parallel attention is given to emerging intellectual property (IP) ambiguities surrounding AI-assisted and AI-generated content, alongside ethical concerns including authenticity, disclosure obligations, deepfake risks, cultural representation, and algorithmic bias. Findings synthesised from contemporary studies indicate functional differentiation rather than simple access gaps: male creators more frequently employ AI for technical and coding-oriented tasks, while female creators concentrate on text generation, creative writing, and aesthetic enhancement (Raza et al., 2026). Persistent gendered risk perceptions regarding societal harms further moderate adoption intensity, particularly among younger women (Stephany & Duszynski, 2026). Malaysia’s human-centred copyright framework under the Copyright Act 1987 leaves significant gaps for AI-generated works, exposing creators, especially those building personal brands, to ownership uncertainty and unauthorised replication of likeness or style (Wardi et al., 2025). The paper proposes an integrated ethical-governance and IP-reform agenda tailored to the Malaysian creator ecosystem and calls for gender-responsive AI literacy programmes, mandatory disclosure standards, and updated guidance from the Malaysian Intellectual Property Organisation (MyIPO). Implications for policy, platform design, and future empirical research are discussed.

articles.title: Dual Exposure: Systematic and Systemic Risk
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: Systemic risk can be measured by the covariance between an institution’s return and the sector return. This allows systemic risk to be decomposed by decomposing the sector return. When the sector return is separated into a market-driven component and a market-orthogonal residual, systemic risk splits into systematic risk, reflecting exposure to the market-driven component, and net systemic risk, reflecting exposure to the residual. We examine how these two risk dimensions relate to financial sector returns, contemporaneously and intertemporally. Using a sample including the 2008 global financial crisis, we find that including both risks explains substantial variation in financial sector returns.

articles.title: Ethical Challenges of Gamification in Healthcare and Health Promotion: A Systematic Thematic Analysis
articles.authors: Nooruldeen Taffar
articles.abstract:
Introduction: the concept of gamification provides possible solutions for the field of healthcare in terms of efficiency, and behavioural change. This work is a trial systematically highlighting the ethical considerations of gamification in healthcare. This research analyses the ethical effects of gamification on healthcare and health approach on a systematic basis.

Methodology: the author follows a thematic analysis-based approach to highlight the themes of ethical challenges facing the implementation of gamification in healthcare and health promotion. This paper follows the PRISMA flow diagram for data collection. SPIDER and CASP checklist are used for search strategy and quality appraisal.

Results and discussion: seven different themes of ethical challenges are identified in the literature including harm, privacy, manipulation and exploitation, inequality and stereotypes encouragement, data ownership, merging of the real and the virtual world, and the change of power dynamics. Such themes interact with each other in a thematic way that highlights a cause-and-effect relationship.

Conclusion: the paper provides an interactive framework of ethical challenges scenarios. The author concludes that the use of different search words presented new themes in comparison to the previous work on the topic and the need for further widening of the scope of research for identification of more themes.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of the Graphic Design Landscape in Malaysia: Implications for Professional Futures and Higher Education Reform
articles.authors: SF Syed Abdul Rahman
articles.abstract:
The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into creative workflows has fundamentally altered the graphic design industry worldwide, with particularly pronounced effects in emerging creative economies such as Malaysia. This article examines how AI technologies have reshaped professional practices, labour dynamics, and creative processes within Malaysia’s graphic design sector. Drawing on recent empirical studies conducted among Malaysian design students and practitioners, the analysis explores efficiency gains, authenticity concerns, cultural representation challenges, and shifts in required competencies (Wong et al., 2025; Artificial Intelligence Integration among Design Students in Malaysia, 2025). Evidence indicates that while GenAI tools accelerate ideation and production, they simultaneously raise questions about originality and the preservation of culturally specific visual languages that characterise Malaysian design practice (Abdullah et al., 2025; Azizi & Sannusi, 2025).
The discussion then addresses the evolving roles of graphic designers, emphasising hybrid human–AI collaboration, conceptual leadership, and cultural fluency as essential future competencies (Zhou et al., 2025; Lestari, 2026). Designers are increasingly required to function as orchestrators of algorithmic outputs rather than sole executors of visual tasks, a shift that demands both technical fluency and critical judgment. Finally, the article evaluates the responsibilities of Malaysian universities in redesigning academic programmes to prepare graduates for an AI-mediated profession. Recommendations include systematic curriculum integration of AI literacy, ethical frameworks, critical design thinking, and industry-aligned experiential learning (Yang, 2025; Bing, 2025). The paper argues that proactive educational reform is essential to ensure that Malaysian designers retain competitive advantage while safeguarding cultural authenticity and professional identity in an increasingly automated creative landscape.

articles.title: Patient Preferences for Non-Opioid Regimens in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A Systematic Review of Discrete Choice Experiments
articles.authors: Ni Wayan Mahahari; Kadek Tania Mediana Putri; Ni Putu Aryati Suryaningsih; Gde Palguna Reganata; Dewa Ayu Putu Satrya Dewi; Kadek Hendra Darmawan
articles.abstract: Chronic non-cancer pain is highly prevalent, and concerns about long-term opioid harms have increased interest in non-opioid therapies. Understanding which treatment attributes patients value is essential for shared decision-making. This systematic review synthesised discrete choice experiments (DCEs) to identify the treatment attributes patients prioritise when choosing non-opioid regimens for chronic non-cancer pain, and to appraise the methodological quality of the underlying studies. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420251273180), we searched nine databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, EconLit, PubMed and the Cochrane Library). Two reviewers independently screened records and assessed methodological quality using a modified ISPOR Conjoint Analysis Good Research Practices checklist. Attributes were classified using the Sain et al. (2020) framework into outcome, process and cost categories, and synthesised narratively. Seventeen studies (1,540 records identified) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing 109 attributes; 88% were industry-funded. Outcome attributes predominated (67.9%), followed by process (25.7%) and cost (6.4%). Clinical effectiveness was the most influential attribute, identified as the primary priority in 57.1% of studies combining all three categories, with safety acting as a key differentiator and cost as a constraint. Most studies met ISPOR standards (scores 10.5 to 12), though visual aids (71%) and direct patient input (18%) were underused. Patients prioritise clinical benefit when choosing non-opioid pain therapies, informing preference-sensitive decision-making, clinical guidelines and health technology assessment.

articles.title: EL ILIBERALISMO COMO OPCIÓN ELECTORAL PARTIDARIA EN EL MUNDO (2000-2019)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: En este texto se acude a los datos de la base de datos por partido del proyecto Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) para el período 2000-2019, utilizando un índice sobre iliberalismo. Del análisis se concluye que la adopción de una actitud iliberal hacia los oponentes responde primordialmente a un posicionamiento en el eje populismo-elitismo, donde lo populista se vincula más comúnmente con lo iliberal, especialmente en el discurso de la derecha. Asumir una posición de ruptura con los principios democrático-liberales resulta claramente redituable en votos y asientos. Esto se refleja en que, mientras sólo el 45% de los partidos liberales participan en gobiernos (menos de una quinta parte como componente mayoritario), el 62% de los partidos con posturas contrarias al respeto a sus contendientes accede al gobierno, siendo el componente mayoritario en más de una tercera parte de las ocasiones.

articles.title: Patient Preferences for Biologic Therapies in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review of Discrete Choice Experiments
articles.authors: Kadek Tania Mediana Putri; Ni Wayan Mahahari; Dewa Ayu Putu Satrya Dewi; Ni Putu Aryati Suryaningsih; Putu Yudhistira Budi Setiawan; Kadek Hendra Darmawan
articles.abstract:
Introduction: Balancing high efficacy against significant toxicity risks a central challenge in biologic therapy selection for chronic diseases. This systematic review evaluated discrete choice experiments (DCEs) of patient preferences for biologic therapy to identify the treatment attributes that most consistently influence patient choice.
Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched (PROSPERO CRD420251271716) for Discrete Choice Experiments (DCEs) evaluating patient preferences for biologic therapies. Two reviewers independently screened eligible studies, extracted study characteristics and treatment attributes, evaluated methodological quality using an ISPOR-based quality assessment instrument, and identified the two most important treatment attributes reported in each study.
Results: Twenty-four studies (2010-2025), most published after 2020, met inclusion criteria across a range of chronic diseases, most frequently psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Of 173 attributes identified, 61% were outcome attributes, 34% process, and 5% cost. Patients most often prioritized the risk of serious adverse events, followed by treatment response; process features gained importance when efficacy and safety differences were minimal, and cost carried greater weight where out-of-pocket expenditure was higher. Twenty-three of 24 studies achieved the maximum ISPOR score of 9/9
Conclusions: Patient preferences in biologic selection follow a clear hierarchy determined by perceived risk, expected benefit, and treatment context. Incorporating these preferences into shared decision-making might improve treatment alignment and long-term patient adherence. This evidence supports patient-centered care and counseling at the initiation of treatment.

articles.title: Political Memes as Participatory Rhetoric for Voter Mobilisation during Elections
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Osa Director Uhunmwenkpenma; Onyeoma Osife-Kurex
articles.abstract: Political communication during elections has increasingly shifted to digital spaces, with political memes emerging as a dominant form of citizen-generated content. This study examined political memes as participatory rhetoric for voter mobilisation during elections in Nigeria. Anchored on Participatory Rhetoric Theory, Framing Theory and Agenda-Setting Theory, the study adopted the library research method. Findings revealed memes framed candidates as “heroes,” “villains” or “incompetent” and such affective frames recorded the highest engagement and correlated significantly with turnout intention. Thematic analysis also showed that viral memes set the agenda for peer political discussion by foregrounding issues such as youth inclusion and insecurity. Thus, the study concluded that political memes function as participatory rhetorical artefacts that simplify electoral issues, foster in-group solidarity and mobilise first-time and apathetic voters beyond elite-controlled campaign channels. However, the circulation of satirical misinformation within memes poses risks to informed participation.

articles.title: AI Incidents and Marginalized Populations: A Descriptive Analysis of the AI Incident Database (1983–2026) from a Social Work Perspective
articles.authors: Nanyi Deng; Sebastian Douglas; Jemel P. Aguilar; Wen Yin
articles.abstract:
Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in the institutional core of social work practice, such as law enforcement, healthcare, education, and public administration. Despite this implementation, the social work profession lacks a population-level empirical baseline of documented AI-related harm. This study characterizes the landscape of documented AI incidents, focusing on marginalized populations and the sectors in which social workers practice.
Method: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of the AI Incident Database (AIID; snapshot as of June 29, 2026), a curated repository of publicly reported AI incidents. The record comprises 1,549 incidents (1983–2026), with three independent post hoc classification systems that provide harm coding for overlapping subsets of these incidents. We report descriptive population proportions with explicit denominators for every reported statistic.
Results: Most incidents (83.8%) were dated 2020 or later, though documented incidents date back to 1983, predating large language models by decades. Among the 214 CSET-coded incidents, a subset weighted toward pre-2020 events, 32.7% involved protected characteristics, most often race or ethnicity. Social-work-relevant sectors, including healthcare, law enforcement, education, and public administration, accounted for 23.4% of these incidents. Incidents in these sectors implicated protected characteristics (50.0% vs. 27.4%) and rights violations (40.0% vs. 4.9%) at markedly higher rates than other sectors, and 80.0% involved the public sector. Among incidents classified by intent and deployment timing, discrimination and toxicity incidents were coded as unintentional in 80.7% of cases, and 97.6% occurred after the AI system was already in active use rather than during development or testing.
Discussion: Documented AI incidents concentrate on the sectors and populations central to social work's mandate. These findings establish an empirical baseline for AI harm surveillance and ground specific advocacy priorities: mandatory incident reporting in publicly funded services, third-party algorithmic auditing, and algorithmic literacy in frontline practice.

articles.title: A scoping review of threats, enabling technologies, and forms of AI involvement associated with child sexual exploitation and abuse
articles.authors: Chad Hemady; Sara Valdebenito; Chanel Hayre; Franziska Meinck; Deborah Fry
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly implicated in child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSEA), but inconsistent terminology has limited synthesis. This scoping review mapped reported AI-CSEA threats and enabling technologies and examined how AI systems participated in perpetration. English-language sources published from January 2010 to 1 April 2026 were eligible if they concerned children under 18 and where an AI system played a material role in the abuse process. Searches of the ACM Digital Library, CINAHL, Web of Science, EBSCOhost databases, and grey literature identified 48 sources. Three reviewers contributed to screening and data charting, and extracted data were summarised numerically and through qualitative content analysis. Overall, our review found that AI-CSEA nomenclature conflated abusive conduct, production methods and system roles. Five non-exclusive threat domains comprised i) AI-generated CSAM, ii) AI-manipulated CSAM, iii) grooming, iv) sextortion, and v) conversational AI sexual abuse. Six technology groups encompassed: i) generative systems; ii) model adaptation and training data; iii) media manipulation systems; iv) conversational systems; v) immersive and embodied technologies; and vi) access, hosting, and distribution infrastructure. Forms of AI involvement include: i) AI-enabled assistance with person-directed abuse; ii) AI-simulated co-production of user-initiated scenarios; and iii) AI-driven initiation or escalation of sexualised conduct. AI-CSEA largely reflected established forms of abuse reshaped by new modes of production and interaction. Existing act-based classifications of violence against children provide a suitable foundation but require supplementary recording of production route, child linkage, system role and point of steering.

articles.title: Record Linkage Error and Inference in Population Research
articles.authors: Casey Breen; Won-tak Joo
articles.abstract: The explosion in digitization of large-scale administrative data and advances in record linkage have opened up new possibilities for studying core topics in population research, including social mobility, early-life determinants of longevity, and shifts in ethnoracial identity. Much attention has been paid to improving record linkage algorithms, but methodological guidance for researchers analyzing linked data is limited. We propose a general framework to explain how different types of linkage errors—false matches and missed matches—impact inference with linked data and introduce a bias-correction method. We then conduct three empirical case studies on canonical topics in population research: social mobility, the education–longevity gradient, and shifts in ethnoracial identification. These case studies demonstrate the settings in which linkage errors do and do not meaningfully impact substantive research findings. We conclude with practical recommendations for researchers performing inference with linked data and provide an accompanying R package implementing the methods introduced in this paper.

articles.title: How Schools Organize the Standard Life Course and Translate It into Relations to the Self
articles.authors: Vance Byun
articles.abstract:
This paper analyzes why the educational success narrative and standard life-course pathway continue to organize Korean schools despite their uneven efficacy, and how this structure is translated into students' self-relations and differentiated suffering. The educational success narrative is defined as the entry point into a standard life-course narrative linking good grades and university admission to stable employment, economic independence, housing, family formation, and old age. It gained institutional distribution during industrialization and educational expansion by organizing experiences of social mobility and stability. Yet higher-education massification, credential expansion, and changes in labor and housing markets have made its efficacy more conditional. School evaluation, family investment, university and labor-market selection, and textbook life-planning representations do not adjust at the same pace. This paper interprets this as a nonsynchronous breakdown rather than its disappearance.

The paper reconstructs mechanisms between macro-level structure and individual suffering often compressed into “internalization.” School structure appears as a distributive grammar in which time, attention, information, opportunities, recognition, and sanctions are attached to particular performances. Through repeated experiences of action and outcome, students develop a practice grammar organizing attention, time, and the body. When external evaluative standards are recursively applied to the self, self-interpellation emerges; when a pathway is experienced as the only route preserving safety, relationships, recognition, dignity, and the future, acute affective linkage forms. Yet structural coercion need not become a criterion of self-worth. Structural entrapment occurs when actors continue to perform because institutional distribution is high and resources for exit are limited even without believing the narrative.

These dimensions are assembled into V-Q-C coordinates to derive five mechanisms of suffering: suffering within the narrative, the double bind, anomie, structural coercion, and guilt induced by attacks on legitimacy. Distributive grammar itself is not treated as an error or violence to be eliminated, but as the institutional and phenomenological horizon through which schools allocate limited time and opportunities and students encounter worldly possibilities and risks. The problem arises when one distributive grammar monopolistically links performance evaluation to love, belonging, dignity, and the whole of life while foreclosing revision, retrying, and alternative pathways. Accordingly, Bildung is redefined as a phenomenological process of self-formation in which one is protected enough to revise one’s horizon of expectation in response to experience. Schools and teachers should limit the scope of evaluation, distinguish institutional advantage from human worth, and preserve the reversibility of failure and relational respect.

articles.title: Who Works from Home, and Who Enjoys It? Gender, Parenthood, and Affective Well-Being in Britain Before, During, and After the Covid-19 Pandemic
articles.authors: zhuofei lu; Matthew Henglong Luo; Yucheng He; Man-Yee Kan
articles.abstract:
Policy discourse in the United Kingdom presents flexible working as a remedy for
work–family conflict, with mothers and carers as its principal beneficiaries. We
ask who actually works from home, and who enjoys it, using UK Time Use Sur-
vey diaries collected before (2014–2015), during (2020–2021), and after (2023)
the Covid-19 pandemic. Uptake is measured as daily minutes of home-based paid
work and as the share of paid work performed at home; affective experience
is measured as episode-level enjoyment, modelled with two-way (person–diary)
fixed effects among non-manual employees on weekday diaries. Working from
home rose sharply during the pandemic and remained elevated in 2023, but
mothers are not its principal users: in 2023 they record the lowest uptake of the
four gender × parenthood groups. The affective evidence is period-dependent.
Before the pandemic, women report lower enjoyment when working at home
than on-site, whereas men report higher. In 2021, under lockdown, this pat-
tern inverts: mothers show the largest positive home-working association of any
group. By 2023 the lockdown pattern is gone: mothers, fathers, and childless
women all report significantly lower enjoyment when working at home, and only childless men report higher. The one period in which mothers benefited was
thus the period in which home-working was a universal mandate rather than a
statutory entitlement. Flexible-working rights alone appear insufficient to deliver
the affective benefits promised to mothers and carers; complementary care and
workplace-norm interventions are required.

articles.title: Educational and Socioeconomic Determinants of Parents’ Knowledge of Child Abuse in Egor Local Government Area of Edo State, Nigeria
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Egwonor Opoggen; Obehi Destiny Elebhosele
articles.abstract: Despite the enactment of the Child Rights Act and the growing advocacy for child protection in Nigeria, child abuse is a huge public health and social welfare problem. Parents have a key role to play in protecting children but their understanding of what is child abuse may be influenced by their education and social and economic status. The study looked both educational and socioeconomic factors influencing parents' knowledge of child abuse in Egor Local Government Area of Edo State, Nigeria. Specifically, the level of parents' knowledge about child abuse and the effect of educational level and socioeconomic status on parents' knowledge were evaluated.
